aiExplanation: This function computes the **sum of the squares of distinct counts** over every contiguous subarray of `nums`. The outer loop fixes a starting index `i`, and for each start it creates a fresh `Set` to track which values have been seen so far. The inner loop extends the subarray one element at a time by moving `j` from `i` to the end, adding `nums[j]` to the set; because a `Set` ignores duplicates, `set.size` at any moment is exactly the number of **distinct values** in the subarray `nums[i..j]`. After each extension, the code adds `set.size ** 2` (the distinct count squared) to the running total `res`. By the time both loops finish, every possible subarray has been visited once, so `res` holds the required answer. The approach runs in **O(n²)** time with **O(n)** extra space for the set.
